QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_45

question.text: Under SAS-500, when assessing an environmental intervention, the SIA's contribution test focuses on:

answer.text: Whether the SE has added new offices
Whether the environmental outcome would have happened in the absence of the project, with deadweight used to avoid overclaiming the SE's contribution

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook frames the assessment in terms of whether evidenced changes are traceable to the intervention, how much could have happened irrespective of the intervention, what would have happened in the absence of the project, and using deadweight to avoid overclaiming. Option C uses this language directly for an environmental indicator. The Trap: Adding offices (A), raising budget (B) and hiring staff (D) describe scale or inputs and do not address whether the outcome would have occurred without the intervention. Note: Document the absence-of-project comparison for each environmental indicator and capture the deadweight reasoning so that the SE's contribution is neither overstated nor unsupported.
